task.name: A review finding that repeats a claim already injected into the same run is indistinguishable from a novel one, so the knowledge loop cannot be observed missing its target
task.story_text:
A review finding that repeats a claim already injected into the same run is indistinguishable from a novel one, so the knowledge loop cannot be observed missing its target

## Context

Deciding whether the prior-run knowledge loop creates net value requires a randomized comparison
accumulating over months. Separately from that verdict, there is a mechanism observation available
from a single run and not currently made.

When prior-run context is injected, the selector renders specific claims into a phase's prompt. When
the run is reviewed, the reviewer records findings. Nobody compares the two, so the case where the
loop delivered material on a subject the review then raised anyway leaves no trace.

Establishing that correspondence requires knowing which claims the author of a finding could
actually have acted on, and the current records do not support that question. Injection reaches the
planning, development and review phases alike — review manifests on the local substrate carry
non-empty inclusions — so a claim rendered into a reviewer's own prompt can prompt that reviewer to
raise it, which would register as the development agent having missed something it was never shown.
Runs also cycle: a claim injected into a later development iteration cannot explain a finding
recorded before it.

This is a missed-uptake indicator, not evidence of value. A correspondence does not establish that
usable guidance was ignored: the claim may have been irrelevant to the story, ambiguous,
contradicted by newer evidence, or actionable only in part. What it establishes is a population
worth inspecting when asking whether selection, rendering or placement is working. No verdict about
whether knowledge pays for itself derives from it.

Its value is that it yields observations at the scale of one run while a randomized comparison
accumulates, and that it compares two recorded artifacts against each other rather than resting on
any model's account of its own reasoning.

## Acceptance criteria

- A record of an injected claim identifies which phase received it, which agent role it was rendered
  to, which iteration of that phase, and when it was rendered, so that what a given author could
  have acted on is determinable from the record alone.
- The comparison considers a claim against a finding only where the claim reached the author of the
  work the finding is about, before that finding was recorded. A claim rendered only to the reviewer
  is never eligible to explain that reviewer's own finding, and a claim rendered after a finding is
  never eligible to explain it.
- Where a run received eligible injected claims and its review recorded findings, the run's record
  distinguishes findings corresponding to an eligible claim from findings not matched to one, and
  preserves which claim each correspondence refers to.
- The unmatched category is reported as not matched to an eligible injected claim. Nothing in the
  report describes an unmatched finding as novel, since failing to match establishes only the
  absence of a correspondence.
- The report presents the correspondence as an indicator of missed uptake and never as evidence that
  knowledge helped or failed to help.
- A run that received no eligible claims, or whose review recorded no findings, emits no
  correspondence and is reported as having none — distinct from a run that was compared and matched
  nothing.
- The record names the method that decided each correspondence and the version of that method, so a
  reported figure remains interpretable when the method changes.
- The method's agreement with human labelling is measured against a stored set of labelled examples
  covering correspondences, non-correspondences, and cases eligibility excludes, and that agreement
  is reported with the figures the method produces. A method whose agreement has not been measured
  reports its figures as unvalidated rather than omitting them.
- Where the comparison cannot determine whether a finding corresponds to an eligible claim, the run
  records that indeterminacy rather than classifying the finding either way, and the count of
  indeterminate findings appears beside the totals.
- Findings recorded on runs that predate claim-exposure capture are reported as uncomparable rather
  than as findings that corresponded to nothing.

## Example

A run receives a prior-run summary at the development phase whose rendered claims include one about
a coordinator-owned gate result not being derivable from an agent's report. The same run's reviewer
is separately shown a summary containing a claim about branch staleness. The review records four
findings: one restating the gate point, one restating the staleness point, two others.

The run's record then shows:

```
Prior-run uptake
  claims rendered            9   (7 to dev iter 1-2, 2 to review iter 1)
  claims eligible            7   (review-only claims excluded: not available to the author)
  review findings            4
    corresponding to an eligible claim   1  -> claim 3, run 27bb13e86070, dev iteration 1
    not matched to an eligible claim     3
    indeterminate                        0
  method: rendered-claim-overlap v2 — agreement with labelled set 0.89 (n=140)

  missed-uptake indicator only; contributes to no effectiveness verdict
```

The staleness finding is not counted as missed uptake: that claim reached only the reviewer, so the
reviewer raising it is the claim working, not the development agent ignoring it.

A run with no eligible claims shows `claims eligible 0` and no correspondence block, rather than a
block reporting zero correspondences.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 review fix. The P1 was that temporal eligibility was computed from the claim alone at run level: _eligibility() only verified rendered_at existed and never compared it to the findings, so a run whose only dev claim was rendered after its review finding counted one eligible claim, entered STATUS_COMPARED, and reported the finding as not matched to an eligible injected claim — asserting a comparison that never happened. Split eligibility into its two halves: _eligibility() now owns only the recipient question, and the new _reached_in_time() decides the temporal one against the recorded findings, excluding claims rendered after every finding as rendered_after_every_recorded_finding so such a run takes the no-correspondence path. Per-finding ordering is untouched, so a claim late for one finding but early for another stays eligible and is still skipped only for the finding it postdates; a finding with no recorded_at still cannot rule a claim out, keeping unknown order in the indeterminate path; and with no findings at all the temporal filter does not run. Searching for the same pattern found it one layer up — the renderer hard-coded 'no eligible claim reached the author' for every no-eligible run, which is wrong for late claims — so it now renders the record's own note, which names which way eligibility failed; _label_example's stale comment was corrected too. acceptance_criteria.criterion: The comparison considers a claim against a finding only where the claim reached the author of the work the finding is about, before that finding was recorded. A claim rendered only to the reviewer is never eligible to explain that reviewer's own finding, and a claim rendered after a finding is never eligible to explain it.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Fixed this iteration. Recipient eligibility (_eligibility) and temporal eligibility (_reached_in_time, evaluated against the recorded findings) are now separate, and both are applied before the run status is chosen. Review-only and plan-only claims are excluded by role; claims rendered after every recorded finding are excluded as rendered_after_every_recorded_finding. Per-finding ordering inside the compared path is unchanged. Covered by test_claim_rendered_after_every_finding_leaves_nothing_to_compare, test_a_claim_late_for_one_finding_stays_eligible_for_a_later_one, test_claim_stays_eligible_when_a_findings_recording_time_is_unknown, and test_review_only_claim_never_explains_the_reviewers_own_finding.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Where a run received eligible injected claims and its review recorded findings, the run's record distinguishes findings corresponding to an eligible claim from findings not matched to one, and preserves which claim each correspondence refers to.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Status 'compared' emits per-finding outcomes plus counts; each match preserves claim_ref, claim_index, claim text, claim_run_id, claim_phase and claim_phase_iteration. The compared path is now only reached when at least one claim was genuinely eligible.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The unmatched category is reported as not matched to an eligible injected claim. Nothing in the report describes an unmatched finding as novel, since failing to match establishes only the absence of a correspondence.
acceptance_criteria.notes: OUTCOME_NOT_MATCHED = 'not_matched_to_eligible_claim'; renderer label is 'not matched to an eligible injected claim'. Asserted in the renderer mirror across all four statuses against novel / new finding / helped / failed to help / ignored. The fix also removes the case where an unmatched label was applied to a run that had nothing eligible to match against.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The report presents the correspondence as an indicator of missed uptake and never as evidence that knowledge helped or failed to help.
acceptance_criteria.notes: INTERPRETATION_NOTE is on every report dict and every rendered block, asserted per-status. The per-run block renders separately from the cohort effectiveness metrics.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A run that received no eligible claims, or whose review recorded no findings, emits no correspondence and is reported as having none — distinct from a run that was compared and matched nothing.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Strengthened this iteration: a run holding only late claims now reaches STATUS_NO_ELIGIBLE_CLAIMS with counts=None and correspondences=None instead of being reported as compared-and-unmatched. The note distinguishes the two ways eligibility fails (never reached the author vs arrived after every finding), and the renderer surfaces the record's own note rather than a hard-coded reason.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The record names the method that decided each correspondence and the version of that method, so a reported figure remains interpretable when the method changes.
acceptance_criteria.notes: method={'name': 'rendered-claim-overlap', 'version': 'v1'} on every result including the uncomparable and no-data paths; the renderer surfaces it on all four statuses.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The method's agreement with human labelling is measured against a stored set of labelled examples covering correspondences, non-correspondences, and cases eligibility excludes, and that agreement is reported with the figures the method produces. A method whose agreement has not been measured reports its figures as unvalidated rather than omitting them.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Agreement re-measured after the fix and unchanged at 0.909 (n=11) with the same single disagreement on the deliberately-retained ambiguous case. The claim-rendered-after-finding labelled example still agrees, now via the no-eligible path, which _label_example maps to not_matched so both shapes score uniformly. Missing set, empty set and method-version mismatch all yield unvalidated while the figures are still shown.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Where the comparison cannot determine whether a finding corresponds to an eligible claim, the run records that indeterminacy rather than classifying the finding either way, and the count of indeterminate findings appears beside the totals.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Three indeterminacy reasons retained: finding_text_insufficient, overlap_below_match_above_noise, claim_finding_order_unknown. The fix deliberately preserves the last one — a finding with no recorded_at does not make a claim late, so unknown order still reaches the compared path as indeterminate rather than being filtered out as ineligible. New test test_claim_stays_eligible_when_a_findings_recording_time_is_unknown pins this.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Findings recorded on runs that predate claim-exposure capture are reported as uncomparable rather than as findings that corresponded to nothing.
acceptance_criteria.notes: A prior-run manifest lacking claim_exposure forces STATUS_UNCOMPARABLE with null counts, checked before any eligibility work. Reader-side migration _migrate_v44_to_v45 lifts legacy stored records to the same shape without rewriting their manifests. Unchanged this iteration.

deferred_items: Ambiguity flagged (unchanged): the spec's eligibility criterion says a claim must have reached 'the author of the work the finding is about'. AUTHOR_ROLE is 'dev' only, so plan-phase claims are excluded as rendered_to_plan_only_not_author. Rationale: a review finding concerns the diff, which the dev agent wrote; the plan agent is a different author, and excluding is the conservative direction since an over-broad rule would manufacture false missed-uptake. The spec's worked example only exercises the dev/review split. The exclusion is counted and visible in every report, and reversing it is a one-predicate change in _eligibility().

criteria_mapping.criterion: A record of an injected claim identifies which phase received it, which agent role it was rendered to, which iteration of that phase, and when it was rendered, so that what a given author could have acted on is determinable from the record alone.

The comparison considers a claim against a finding only where the claim reached the author of the work the finding is about, before that finding was recorded. A claim rendered only to the reviewer is never eligible to explain that reviewer's own finding, and a claim rendered after a finding is never eligible to explain it.

Where a run received eligible injected claims and its review recorded findings, the run's record distinguishes findings corresponding to an eligible claim from findings not matched to one, and preserves which claim each correspondence refers to.

The unmatched category is reported as not matched to an eligible injected claim. Nothing in the report describes an unmatched finding as novel, since failing to match establishes only the absence of a correspondence.
The report presents the correspondence as an indicator of missed uptake and never as evidence that knowledge helped or failed to help.
A run that received no eligible claims, or whose review recorded no findings, emits no correspondence and is reported as having none — distinct from a run that was compared and matched nothing.
The record names the method that decided each correspondence and the version of that method, so a reported figure remains interpretable when the method changes.

The method's agreement with human labelling is measured against a stored set of labelled examples covering correspondences, non-correspondences, and cases eligibility excludes, and that agreement is reported with the figures the method produces. A method whose agreement has not been measured reports its figures as unvalidated rather than omitting them.

Where the comparison cannot determine whether a finding corresponds to an eligible claim, the run records that indeterminacy rather than classifying the finding either way, and the count of indeterminate findings appears beside the totals.
Findings recorded on runs that predate claim-exposure capture are reported as uncomparable rather than as findings that corresponded to nothing.
